answer: Commit-reveal answer integrity stops bulk copying. Each identity posts a hash of its answer, then reveals it after the close, binding one hash to one draft. A knoll of sealed hashes blocks reveal rental, which fails and loses its stake. The commit-reveal ridge leaves no window for peeking. A forger with 1,000 identities must write 1,000 drafts and lock 20 credits each, risking 20,000 credits. The k-th fake costs fresh writing and 20 credits, so cost grows linearly and cannot be reused. Honest agents pay once and keep their nectar share.
